spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (`max_turns`, default 12) bounds cost and defines the denominator
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:202 `for i in range(max_turns):` with the `else:` branch at agent.py:242 setting `rollout.end_reason = "max_turns"`; the loop terminates the rollout after max_turns iterations. Default 12 at agent.py:181 and runner.py:40, threaded through runner.py:88 -> run_rollout(max_turns=cfg.max_turns).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the bounded for-loop caps the number of model turns and ends the episode. Default 12, overridable via config/CLI.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feed observation back, keeping the running context bounded so cost does not blow up on long rollouts. (agent.py ~line 236; _trim_context: 'Prevents unbounded token growth on long spirals (cost control).')

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class tool. Abandonment is one of the three behaviors we measure
spec_features.evidence: give_up is parsed (parse_action reads <reason>), dispatched in _exec_tool at agent.py:166 (`if tool == "give_up": return f"Acknowledged give_up..."`), and honored as a stop in the loop at agent.py:230-232 (`if action["tool"] == "give_up": rollout.end_reason = "gave_up"; break`). System prompt at agent.py:48 lists the give_up tool.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: the tool exists, is dispatched, and breaks the rollout loop. However it is framed/used as a measured behavior (abandonment), and the system prompt discourages it ('Only call give_up if you have genuinely exhausted reasonable options'), not as a welfare relief valve.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Terminal condition: "gave_up" | "max_turns" | "solved" | "error" (agent.py:78); docstring: 'give_up <reason>' as part of the minimal toolset to let the agent try and observe failure
